card: Switches native Windows builds and CI from MSVC (cl.exe) to clang-cl, dropping support for cl.exe. Native builds with cl.exe lacked inline assembly support on x64/ARM64 and regularly required workarounds for compiler bugs and internal errors (#31456, #36153). Author benchmarks report block connection throughput increasing by ~55–60% and Windows CI build time dropping by 38%. Developers building natively on Windows must install the Clang C++ tools and use Visual Studio 18.7 or newer.
changed_since_previous: No conceptual change to the toolchain switch; refines warning cleanups in CMake introspection tests so they pass with strict `-Werror` enforcement, and renames the Windows build documentation.

enables: Hardware-accelerated inline assembly optimizations on Windows (e.g., secp256k1 #1681)

evidence: Author benchmarks report block connection throughput increasing from ~7.4 to ~11.5–11.8 block/s (~55–60% speedup) and deserialization tests improving by ~55% when switching from MSVC to clang-cl.
Author CI timing demonstrates a 38% reduction in Windows CI build times (from 20m 35s with MSVC to 12m 43s with clang-cl).
PR description notes closing #31456 and #36153, and addressing #14118.
problem: Native Windows compilation with `cl.exe` lacks inline assembly support on x64 and ARM64, runs slower on CI, generates slower binaries, and creates maintenance burden due to MSVC-specific compiler bugs and internal compiler errors (#31456, #36153).

risk.why: Changing the Windows compiler toolchain could break native Windows developer builds or introduce compiler-specific code generation regressions.

scope_notes: Changes build flags across CMake files, alters introspection tests to be warning-free under -Werror, and renames build documentation from build-windows-msvc.md to build-windows-native.md.
summary: Switches native Windows builds and CI from MSVC (`cl.exe`) to Clang (`clang-cl.exe`), completely dropping support for compiling with `cl.exe`. CMake presets, compiler flags, and feature introspection tests are updated for Clang's MSVC-compatible frontend, including linking Clang's runtime builtins library for 128-bit operations. Several MSVC-specific workarounds (such as non-`constexpr` byte swaps and requires-expression limitations) are removed, and the minimum Visual Studio version is bumped to 18.7.
